q: What is the maximum number of repositories allowed per AWS account in CodeCommit by default?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1,000 is not the default limit for CodeCommit repositories.
exp.b: Correct. The default maximum is 5,000 repositories per AWS account, and this limit can be increased via Service Quotas.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10,000 exceeds the default limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 500 is too low; the actual default is 5,000.

q: What is the maximum number of files allowed in a single commit in AWS CodeCommit?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 50.
exp.b: Incorrect. 200 exceeds the actual limit.
exp.c: Correct. AWS CodeCommit allows a maximum of 100 files in a single commit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 500 is far above the actual limit of 100.

q: What is the maximum number of open pull requests allowed in a CodeCommit repository?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 500.
exp.b: Incorrect. 2,000 exceeds the actual maximum.
exp.c: Correct. CodeCommit allows a maximum of 1,000 open pull requests per repository.
exp.d: Incorrect. 100 is too low; the actual limit is 1,000.

q: What is the maximum number of references allowed in a single push to CodeCommit?

exp.a: Incorrect. The actual limit is 4,000.
exp.b: Correct. A maximum of 4,000 references (create, delete, and update) are allowed in a single push, with no limit on the overall number of references in the repository.
exp.c: Incorrect. 1,000 is below the actual limit.
exp.d: Incorrect. 10,000 exceeds the actual limit of 4,000.

q: What availability SLA do AWS CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodePipeline, and CodeDeploy maintain?

exp.a: Incorrect. The SLA is higher than 99.0%.
exp.b: Incorrect. While they exceed 99.9%, the stated SLA commitment is 99.9%.
exp.c: Correct. All four Code* services maintain a 99.9% uptime SLA.
exp.d: Incorrect. The stated SLA is 99.9%, not 99.95%.

q: Which underlying AWS services does CodeCommit use to store customer data redundantly?

exp.a: Incorrect. EBS and RDS are not the storage backends for CodeCommit.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodePipeline, and CodeDeploy use Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB to store customer data redundantly across multiple facilities.
exp.c: Incorrect. EFS and Aurora are not used for this purpose.
exp.d: Incorrect. Glacier and Redshift are not used as backend storage for Code* services.

q: In how many AWS regions is CodeCommit currently available?

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeCommit is available in more regions.
exp.b: Incorrect. The number is higher than 25.
exp.c: Correct. AWS CodeCommit is currently available in 29 regions.
exp.d: Incorrect. 32 exceeds the current availability.

q: What is the default timeout for a CodeDeploy deployment action in CodePipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. 1 day is not the timeout for CodeDeploy actions.
exp.b: Incorrect. 3 days is the timeout for CloudFormation deployment actions, not CodeDeploy.
exp.c: Correct. CodeDeploy and CodeDeploy ECS (blue/green) deployment actions have a 5-day timeout.
exp.d: Incorrect. 7 days exceeds the actual timeout.

q: What is the default timeout for a CloudFormation deployment action in CodePipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudFormation deployment actions have a longer timeout.
exp.b: Correct. CloudFormation deployment actions have a default timeout of 3 days.
exp.c: Incorrect. 5 days is the timeout for CodeDeploy actions.
exp.d: Incorrect. 7 days is not a valid timeout for any standard CodePipeline action.

q: What is the default timeout for an AWS Lambda invoke action in CodePipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. The Lambda invoke action timeout is longer than 1 hour.
exp.b: Incorrect. 12 hours is not the correct timeout.
exp.c: Correct. AWS Lambda invoke actions in CodePipeline have a 24-hour timeout.
exp.d: Incorrect. 48 hours exceeds the actual Lambda invoke action timeout.

q: Which regions are planned for CodeCommit expansion starting Q3 2026?

exp.a: Incorrect. These regions are not mentioned in the expansion plans.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit will expand to eu-south-2 and ca-west-1 starting Q3 2026.
exp.c: Incorrect. These are not the planned expansion regions.
exp.d: Incorrect. These regions don't exist or aren't mentioned in the plans.

q: Why did AWS reverse the de-emphasis of CodeCommit and return it to full General Availability?

opts.a: Regulatory requirements forced AWS to maintain the service
opts.b: Customer feedback showed CodeCommit is a critical piece of infrastructure with deep IAM integration and VPC endpoint support
opts.d: CodeCommit was generating more revenue than expected

exp.a: Incorrect. While regulated industries benefit, it wasn't a regulatory mandate.
exp.b: Correct. AWS listened to customer feedback highlighting CodeCommit's value through IAM integration, VPC endpoint support, CloudTrail logging, and seamless connectivity with CodePipeline and CodeBuild.
exp.c: Incorrect. The decision was based on customer feedback, not competitor pressure.
exp.d: Incorrect. Revenue was not cited as the reason.

q: When was the CodeCommit de-emphasis originally announced?

exp.a: Incorrect. The announcement was later in 2024.
exp.b: Correct. AWS announced plans to de-emphasize CodeCommit in July 2024.
exp.c: Incorrect. November 2025 is when the reversal was announced.
exp.d: Incorrect. March 2025 is not the correct date.

q: How does CodeBuild handle scaling?

opts.a: It requires manual provisioning of build servers
opts.b: It scales up and down dynamically to meet build volume
opts.c: It uses reserved instances for consistent capacity
opts.d: It requires Auto Scaling groups to be configured manually

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeBuild is fully managed and doesn't require manual provisioning.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild scales up and down dynamically to meet your build volume automatically.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodeBuild doesn't use reserved instances.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodeBuild handles scaling automatically without manual ASG configuration.

q: How does CodePipeline increase workflow speed?

opts.a: By using dedicated hardware for each pipeline
opts.c: By caching all build artifacts locally

exp.a: Incorrect. CodePipeline doesn't use dedicated hardware.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline allows you to run actions in parallel to increase workflow speeds.
exp.c: Incorrect. While artifact caching exists, parallel actions are the primary speed mechanism.
exp.d: Incorrect. Pre-compilation is not a CodePipeline feature.

q: Is there a limit on the overall number of references in a CodeCommit repository?

opts.c: No, there is no limit on the overall number of references

exp.a: Incorrect. There is no overall limit on references.
exp.b: Incorrect. There is no overall limit.
exp.c: Correct. While there is a limit of 4,000 references per push, there is no limit on the overall number of references in the repository.
exp.d: Incorrect. 4,000 is the per-push limit, not an overall limit.

q: Can the default CodeCommit repository limit of 5,000 per account be increased?

opts.a: No, it is a hard limit
opts.c: Yes, but only with Enterprise Support
opts.d: No, you must create a new AWS account

exp.a: Incorrect. This limit can be changed.
exp.b: Correct. The 5,000 repository limit can be increased by requesting a service quota increase through AWS Service Quotas.
exp.c: Incorrect. Service Quotas is available to all customers, not just Enterprise Support.
exp.d: Incorrect. You can request a limit increase without creating a new account.

q: A company wants to migrate their polling-based GitHub source pipelines to a more efficient event-driven approach. What should they migrate to?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch Events polling is not the recommended approach.
exp.b: Correct. AWS recommends migrating polling pipelines to webhooks for GitHub source actions.
exp.c: Incorrect. SNS is not the mechanism for GitHub source detection.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda scheduled functions are not the replacement for polling.

q: A team in a regulated industry needs a code repository with deep IAM integration, VPC endpoint support, and CloudTrail logging. Which service best meets these requirements?

exp.a: Incorrect. GitHub doesn't offer native IAM integration or VPC endpoints.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit provides deep IAM integration, VPC endpoint support, CloudTrail logging, and seamless connectivity with other AWS services, making it ideal for regulated industries.
exp.c: Incorrect. Bitbucket Cloud doesn't have native AWS IAM integration.
exp.d: Incorrect. GitLab SaaS doesn't offer native IAM or VPC endpoint support.

q: Your CodePipeline has a Lambda invoke action that has been running for 20 hours. What is the status of this action?

opts.b: It is still running within the timeout period
opts.c: It will timeout in exactly 4 hours

exp.a: Incorrect. The timeout is 24 hours, so 20 hours is still within the limit.
exp.b: Correct. Lambda invoke actions have a 24-hour timeout, so at 20 hours the action is still running within its allowed time.
exp.c: Correct that it has 4 hours remaining, but option B better describes the current status.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda actions do have a 24-hour timeout.

q: A developer is trying to push 5,000 reference updates in a single push to CodeCommit. What will happen?

opts.b: The push will fail because it exceeds the 4,000 reference limit per push
opts.c: The push will partially succeed with only 4,000 references
opts.d: CodeCommit will automatically split it into multiple pushes

exp.a: Incorrect. 5,000 exceeds the 4,000 per-push limit.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit has a maximum of 4,000 references per single push, so 5,000 will fail.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodeCommit doesn't partially process pushes in this manner.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodeCommit doesn't automatically split pushes.

q: A team wants to include 150 files in a single commit to CodeCommit. What should they do?

opts.a: Proceed normally as the limit is 200 files
opts.b: Split the commit into two separate commits since the limit is 100 files per commit
opts.d: Use Git LFS to bypass the limit

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is 100 files, not 200.
exp.b: Correct. Since CodeCommit has a maximum of 100 files per commit, the team must split 150 files into at least two commits.
exp.c: Incorrect. The file-per-commit limit is not adjustable via Service Quotas.
exp.d: Incorrect. Git LFS doesn't bypass the file count per commit limit.

q: Your organization has 4,800 repositories in CodeCommit and needs to create 300 more. What should you do?

opts.b: Delete old repositories to make room
opts.c: Request a service quota increase through AWS Service Quotas
opts.d: It's not possible to have more than 5,000 repositories

exp.a: Incorrect. While possible, requesting a quota increase is simpler.
exp.b: Incorrect. Deleting repositories is unnecessary when you can increase the quota.
exp.c: Correct. The 5,000 repository limit can be increased by requesting a service quota increase.
exp.d: Incorrect. The limit can be changed via Service Quotas.

q: A CodeDeploy deployment action in CodePipeline has been running for 4 days. Should you be concerned?

opts.a: Yes, it has exceeded its timeout
opts.b: No, it still has 1 day before timeout
opts.c: Yes, CodeDeploy actions timeout after 3 days
opts.d: No, CodeDeploy actions have no timeout

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeDeploy actions have a 5-day timeout.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy deployment actions have a 5-day timeout, so at 4 days it still has 1 day remaining.
exp.c: Incorrect. 3 days is the CloudFormation action timeout, not CodeDeploy.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodeDeploy actions do have a 5-day timeout.

q: Which of the following is NOT a feature that makes CodeCommit valuable for regulated industries?

exp.a: Incorrect. IAM integration is a key feature for regulated industries.
exp.b: Incorrect. VPC endpoint support is a valued feature.
exp.c: Correct. Built-in code review AI is not mentioned as a CodeCommit feature for regulated industries.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudTrail logging is a key compliance feature.

q: Which type of source control system is AWS CodeCommit?

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeCommit is not SVN-based.
exp.b: Correct. AWS CodeCommit is an integrated Git repository service.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodeCommit uses Git, not Mercurial.
exp.d: Incorrect. CodeCommit is Git-based, not Perforce.

q: Who is responsible for the performance of AWS Code* services?

exp.a: Incorrect. As fully managed services, AWS is responsible for performance.
exp.b: Correct. AWS services are fully managed, and service teams are responsible for the performance of the services.
exp.c: Incorrect. These are first-party AWS services.
exp.d: Incorrect. AWS service teams bear the responsibility for service performance.

q: What is the nature of CodePipeline quotas related to Region availability and naming constraints?

opts.a: They are soft limits that can be increased
opts.b: They are fixed and cannot be changed
opts.d: They can be changed with Enterprise Support

exp.a: Incorrect. Region availability and naming constraint quotas are fixed.
exp.b: Correct. Quotas related to Region availability, naming constraints, and allowed artifact sizes in CodePipeline are fixed and cannot be changed.
exp.c: Incorrect. These quotas are consistent across all account types.
exp.d: Incorrect. Even Enterprise Support cannot change these fixed quotas.

q: A team wants to build a CI/CD pipeline entirely within AWS. Which combination of services provides source control, build, and deployment?

exp.a: Correct. CodeCommit handles source control, CodeBuild handles building/testing, and CodeDeploy handles deployment. CodePipeline orchestrates the entire workflow.
exp.b: Incorrect. While these can be part of a CI/CD pipeline, they don't form a complete CI/CD toolchain.
exp.c: Incorrect. These are container services, not CI/CD tools.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudWatch and Systems Manager are monitoring/management tools, not CI/CD.

q: What orchestrates the flow between CodeCommit, CodeBuild, and CodeDeploy in a CI/CD pipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. Step Functions is for general workflow orchestration, not CI/CD specifically.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline orchestrates the continuous delivery flow between source, build, and deploy stages.
exp.c: Incorrect. EventBridge can trigger pipelines but doesn't orchestrate the CI/CD flow.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda can be invoked within a pipeline but doesn't orchestrate it.

q: A company needs to deploy their application to both EC2 instances and on-premises servers. Which AWS service supports this?

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeBuild is for building, not deploying to instances.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy supports deployment to EC2 instances, on-premises servers, Lambda functions, and ECS services.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodeCommit is for source code management.
exp.d: Incorrect. CloudFormation is for infrastructure provisioning, not application deployment.

q: What deployment strategy does CodeDeploy support for ECS services?

exp.a: Incorrect. ECS deployments via CodeDeploy use Blue/Green.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy supports Blue/Green deployments for ECS services.
exp.c: Incorrect. While canary is a traffic shifting option, the deployment type is Blue/Green.
exp.d: Incorrect. In-place is for EC2/on-premises, not ECS.

q: When did AWS announce that CodeCommit is returning to full General Availability?

exp.a: Incorrect. July 2024 was when de-emphasis was announced.
exp.b: Incorrect. The announcement came later in 2025.
exp.c: Correct. The blog post announcing CodeCommit's return to full GA was published on 24 November 2025.
exp.d: Incorrect. The announcement was in November 2025.

q: A developer wants to trigger a CodePipeline execution whenever code is pushed to a CodeCommit repository. What mechanism should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. Manual approval requires human intervention.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline uses Amazon EventBridge rules to detect changes in CodeCommit and automatically trigger pipeline executions.
exp.c: Incorrect. Polling is the legacy approach; event-driven is recommended.
exp.d: Incorrect. While SNS can be used for notifications, EventBridge rules trigger pipelines.

q: Which of the following is a valid CodeDeploy deployment type for EC2 instances?

exp.a: Incorrect. EC2 instances support both In-place and Blue/Green.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy supports both In-place and Blue/Green deployment types for EC2 instances.
exp.c: Incorrect. Rolling is not a CodeDeploy deployment type.
exp.d: Incorrect. Canary is a traffic routing option within Blue/Green, not a deployment type.

q: What is the CodeDeploy agent used for?

opts.a: Building source code on EC2 instances
opts.b: Running deployments on EC2 and on-premises instances

exp.a: Incorrect. Building code is CodeBuild's function.
exp.b: Correct. The CodeDeploy agent is installed on EC2 and on-premises instances to enable CodeDeploy to run deployments on them.
exp.c: Incorrect. Git repositories are managed by CodeCommit.
exp.d: Incorrect. Pipeline orchestration is CodePipeline's function.

q: In CodeBuild, what file defines the build commands and settings?

exp.a: Incorrect. Dockerfile is for container image building.
exp.b: Correct. The buildspec.yml file defines the build commands, environment variables, and artifacts for CodeBuild.
exp.c: Incorrect. pipeline.json is not a standard CodeBuild configuration file.
exp.d: Incorrect. appspec.yml is used by CodeDeploy, not CodeBuild.

q: In CodeDeploy, what file specifies the deployment instructions?

exp.a: Incorrect. buildspec.yml is used by CodeBuild.
exp.b: Incorrect. deploy.json is not a standard CodeDeploy file.
exp.c: Correct. The appspec.yml (Application Specification) file defines the deployment actions and lifecycle hooks for CodeDeploy.
exp.d: Incorrect. taskdef.json is an ECS task definition file.

q: A team wants their build environment to match their production environment exactly. What CodeBuild feature should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. Managed environments are pre-configured and may not match production.
exp.b: Correct. Custom Docker images allow teams to create build environments that exactly replicate their production environment.
exp.c: Incorrect. Build badges show build status, not environment configuration.
exp.d: Incorrect. Build caching speeds up builds but doesn't define the environment.

q: Which CodeDeploy lifecycle hook runs before the application is installed?

exp.a: Incorrect. AfterInstall runs after installation.
exp.b: Correct. BeforeInstall runs before the application revision is installed, used for tasks like decrypting files or creating backups.
exp.c: Incorrect. ApplicationStart runs after the application is installed.
exp.d: Incorrect. ValidateService is the last hook to verify the deployment was successful.

q: What are the phases in a CodeBuild buildspec.yml file?

exp.a: Incorrect. These are not the correct buildspec phases.
exp.b: Correct. The buildspec.yml supports install, pre_build, build, and post_build phases.
exp.c: Incorrect. These are not valid buildspec phase names.
exp.d: Incorrect. These are not the correct phase names.

q: A company needs a human to review changes before deploying to production. Which CodePipeline feature should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. Parallel actions run multiple actions simultaneously but don't require approval.
exp.b: Correct. Manual approval actions pause the pipeline and require human approval before proceeding to the next stage.
exp.c: Incorrect. CloudWatch alarms can stop deployments but don't require human review.
exp.d: Incorrect. Source polling is for detecting code changes.

q: Which AWS service provides notifications about events in CodePipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. SES is for email sending but isn't directly integrated with CodePipeline notifications.
exp.b: Correct. Amazon SNS is used to send notifications about pipeline events like stage transitions, approvals, and failures.
exp.c: Incorrect. SQS is for message queuing, not notifications.
exp.d: Incorrect. Config is for resource configuration tracking.

q: Your CodeBuild project needs to access resources in a private VPC. What must you configure?

opts.b: VPC configuration in the CodeBuild project (subnet, security group)
opts.c: A public IP address for the build environment

exp.a: Incorrect. An Internet Gateway doesn't grant access to private resources.
exp.b: Correct. You must configure VPC settings (VPC ID, subnets, and security groups) in the CodeBuild project to access private VPC resources.
exp.c: Incorrect. A public IP doesn't help access private VPC resources.
exp.d: Incorrect. Direct Connect is for on-premises connectivity, not CodeBuild VPC access.

q: Where does CodePipeline store pipeline artifacts between stages?

exp.a: Incorrect. EBS is block storage for EC2, not used for pipeline artifacts.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline uses Amazon S3 buckets (artifact stores) to pass artifacts between stages.
exp.c: Incorrect. EFS is not used for pipeline artifact storage.
exp.d: Incorrect. DynamoDB is used for metadata, not artifact storage.

q: A team has their source code on GitHub but wants to use AWS services for build and deploy. Which pipeline configuration is correct?

opts.a: Source: GitHub, Build: CodeBuild, Deploy: CodeDeploy
opts.b: Source: CodeCommit, Build: Jenkins, Deploy: CodeDeploy
opts.c: Source: S3, Build: CodeBuild, Deploy: CloudFormation
opts.d: Source: GitHub, Build: Lambda, Deploy: ECS

exp.a: Correct. CodePipeline supports GitHub as a source provider, CodeBuild for building, and CodeDeploy for deployment.
exp.b: Incorrect. The requirement is GitHub as source, not CodeCommit.
exp.c: Incorrect. S3 as source doesn't match the GitHub requirement.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lambda is not a build service in this context.

q: Which CodeDeploy deployment configuration deploys to one instance at a time?

exp.a: Incorrect. AllAtOnce deploys to all instances simultaneously.
exp.b: Correct. OneAtATime deploys to one instance at a time, proceeding to the next only after the current one succeeds.
exp.c: Incorrect. HalfAtATime deploys to half the instances at once.
exp.d: Incorrect. Linear10Percent is for Lambda/ECS traffic shifting.

q: What compute types are available in AWS CodeBuild?

exp.a: Incorrect. These are not the official naming conventions.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild offers build.general1.small, build.general1.medium, build.general1.large, and build.general1.2xlarge compute types.
exp.c: Incorrect. These are EC2 instance types, not CodeBuild compute types.
exp.d: Incorrect. These are pricing models, not compute types.

q: You need to encrypt your CodeCommit repository data at rest. What does AWS use by default?

exp.a: Incorrect. By default, AWS managed keys are used, though customers can use CMKs.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit automatically encrypts repository data at rest using AWS managed keys in AWS KMS.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodeCommit always encrypts data at rest.
exp.d: Incorrect. SSL/TLS is for data in transit, not at rest.

q: What encryption does CodeCommit use for data in transit?

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeCommit encrypts all data in transit.
exp.b: Correct. CodeCommit supports both SSH and HTTPS protocols for encrypting data in transit.
exp.c: Incorrect. IPSec VPN is not the primary transport mechanism.
exp.d: Incorrect. While PrivateLink/VPC endpoints are supported, SSH and HTTPS are the standard protocols.

q: Your organization requires all CodeCommit access to remain within the private network without traversing the internet. What should you configure?

exp.a: Incorrect. NAT Gateway still routes through the internet.
exp.b: Correct. VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) for CodeCommit allow private connectivity without internet traversal.
exp.c: Incorrect. Internet Gateway routes traffic through the public internet.
exp.d: Incorrect. Transit Gateway connects VPCs but doesn't provide private service access.

q: Which service logs all API calls made to CodeCommit for auditing purposes?

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudWatch Logs stores application logs, not API call records.
exp.b: Correct. AWS CloudTrail logs all API calls made to CodeCommit, providing an audit trail.
exp.c: Incorrect. AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes.
exp.d: Incorrect. GuardDuty is for threat detection.

q: A CodePipeline CloudFormation deployment action has been running for 72 hours. What happens next?

opts.b: It times out immediately since it's exceeded 3 days
opts.c: It has 2 more days before timeout

exp.a: Incorrect. CloudFormation actions have a 3-day (72-hour) timeout.
exp.b: Correct. CloudFormation deployment actions have a 3-day timeout, and at 72 hours the action will time out.
exp.c: Incorrect. 5 days is the CodeDeploy timeout, not CloudFormation's.
exp.d: Incorrect. Timed out actions are not automatically retried.

q: What are the valid source providers for AWS CodePipeline?

opts.b: CodeCommit, S3, GitHub, Bitbucket, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab

exp.a: Incorrect. This list is incomplete.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline supports CodeCommit, S3, GitHub (via OAuth and GitHub App), Bitbucket, GitHub Enterprise, and GitLab as source providers.
exp.c: Incorrect. CodePipeline supports many more source providers.
exp.d: Incorrect. Only specific providers are supported as source actions.

q: What is the maximum number of stages allowed in a single CodePipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. You can have more than 10 stages.
exp.b: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 20.
exp.c: Correct. CodePipeline allows a maximum of 50 stages per pipeline.
exp.d: Incorrect. There is a fixed limit of 50 stages.

q: What is the maximum number of actions per stage in CodePipeline?

exp.a: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 20.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline allows up to 50 actions per stage.
exp.c: Incorrect. 10 is too low.
exp.d: Incorrect. The limit is 50, not 30.

q: Your team uses CodeBuild and wants to cache dependencies between builds to reduce build time. What caching option should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeBuild supports caching.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild supports S3 caching (stores cache in S3) and local caching (stores cache on the build host) to speed up subsequent builds.
exp.c: Incorrect. EBS volumes are not used for CodeBuild caching.
exp.d: Incorrect. ElastiCache is not integrated with CodeBuild for build caching.

q: How is CodeBuild priced?

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeBuild doesn't charge a flat monthly fee.
exp.b: Correct. CodeBuild charges per minute of compute time used during your builds.
exp.c: Incorrect. Pricing is based on time, not number of builds.
exp.d: Incorrect. Lines of code is not a billing metric.

q: How is CodePipeline priced?

exp.a: Incorrect. CodePipeline charges per pipeline, not per minute.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline charges per active pipeline per month (V1 type) or per action execution (V2 type).
exp.c: Incorrect. Pricing is not based on the number of stages.
exp.d: Incorrect. Pricing is per pipeline, not per deployment.

q: A team wants to run unit tests, integration tests, and security scans in parallel during the Test stage. How should they configure CodePipeline?

opts.b: Create three parallel actions within the same stage
opts.d: Use a single action with all three tasks

exp.a: Incorrect. Separate pipelines add unnecessary complexity.
exp.b: Correct. CodePipeline supports parallel actions within a stage, allowing unit tests, integration tests, and security scans to run simultaneously.
exp.c: Incorrect. Sequential stages would increase pipeline duration.
exp.d: Incorrect. Combining all tasks in one action limits parallelism and makes failures harder to identify.

q: What is the CodeCommit pricing model for the free tier?

opts.b: 5 active users per month, 50 GB storage, 10,000 Git requests

exp.a: Incorrect. CodeCommit has a free tier.
exp.b: Correct. The CodeCommit free tier includes 5 active users per month, 50 GB-month of storage, and 10,000 Git requests per month.
exp.c: Incorrect. The free tier is not limited to one repository.
exp.d: Incorrect. The free tier is ongoing, not a 30-day trial.

q: Which CodeBuild feature allows you to display the build status on your repository?

exp.a: Incorrect. Build notifications alert users but don't display status on the repository.
exp.b: Correct. Build badges provide an embeddable image (passing/failing) that can be displayed on your repository README or webpage.
exp.c: Incorrect. Build reports provide test and coverage details but aren't embeddable status indicators.
exp.d: Incorrect. Build logs show detailed output but aren't visual status indicators.

q: A company wants to gradually shift traffic from the old version to the new version during a Lambda deployment. Which CodeDeploy configuration should they use?

exp.a: Incorrect. AllAtOnce shifts all traffic immediately without gradual shifting.
exp.b: Correct. LambdaCanary10Percent5Minutes shifts 10% of traffic to the new version initially, then shifts the remaining 90% after 5 minutes if no errors occur.
exp.c: Incorrect. OneAtATime is for EC2/on-premises deployments.
exp.d: Incorrect. HalfAtATime is for EC2/on-premises deployments.

q: What is the maximum individual file size that can be stored in a CodeCommit repository?

opts.c: No specific limit beyond Git's inherent limits

exp.a: Incorrect. 2 GB is the total repository size recommendation, not individual file size.
exp.b: Correct. The maximum size of a single file in a CodeCommit API operation (such as PutFile) is 6 MB.
exp.c: Incorrect. There is a specific limit on file size for API operations.
exp.d: Incorrect. 100 MB is not the correct file size limit for CodeCommit API operations.

q: Your CodeDeploy deployment is failing because instances are not being detected. What is the most likely cause?

opts.b: The CodeDeploy agent is not installed or running on the instances
opts.c: The pipeline has too many stages
opts.d: The S3 bucket is in the wrong region

exp.a: Incorrect. buildspec.yml is for CodeBuild, not CodeDeploy.
exp.b: Correct. The CodeDeploy agent must be installed and running on EC2/on-premises instances for CodeDeploy to communicate with and deploy to them.
exp.c: Incorrect. The number of pipeline stages doesn't affect instance detection.
exp.d: Incorrect. While region matters, the most common cause is a missing agent.

q: Which CodeDeploy traffic shifting option shifts traffic in equal increments over time?

exp.a: Incorrect. Canary shifts a small percentage first, then all remaining traffic at once.
exp.b: Correct. Linear deployment shifts traffic in equal increments with an equal number of minutes between each increment.
exp.c: Incorrect. AllAtOnce shifts all traffic immediately.
exp.d: Incorrect. Rolling is not a CodeDeploy traffic shifting option.

q: What is the maximum number of pipelines per region per account in CodePipeline by default?

exp.a: Incorrect. The default limit is higher than 100.
exp.b: Incorrect. 300 is not the default limit.
exp.c: Incorrect. The limit is higher than 500.
exp.d: Correct. The default maximum number of pipelines per region per account in CodePipeline is 1,000.

q: A team wants to automatically rollback a CodeDeploy deployment if a CloudWatch alarm triggers. What should they configure?

opts.a: Manual approval action in the pipeline
opts.b: Automatic rollback configuration with CloudWatch alarm in the deployment group
opts.c: Lambda function to monitor and rollback
opts.d: SNS notification to alert the team

exp.a: Incorrect. Manual approval requires human intervention and doesn't automate rollback.
exp.b: Correct. CodeDeploy supports automatic rollback when a specified CloudWatch alarm is triggered, configured in the deployment group settings.
exp.c: Incorrect. While possible, native CodeDeploy alarm-based rollback is simpler.
exp.d: Incorrect. SNS notifications alert the team but don't automatically rollback.

q: Which CodeBuild environment variable provides the unique build ID?

exp.a: Incorrect. BUILD_NUMBER provides the build number, not the unique ID.
exp.b: Correct. CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID provides the unique identifier for the build in the format project-name:build-ID.
exp.c: Incorrect. PROJECT_NAME provides only the project name.
exp.d: Incorrect. SOURCE_VERSION provides the source version (commit ID or branch).

q: You want to build Docker images in CodeBuild and push them to Amazon ECR. What must be enabled in the build environment?

exp.a: Incorrect. GPU acceleration is not needed for Docker builds.
exp.b: Correct. Privileged mode must be enabled in the CodeBuild environment to build Docker images, as it allows access to the Docker daemon.
exp.c: Incorrect. VPC configuration is for accessing private resources, not Docker builds.
exp.d: Incorrect. S3 caching speeds up builds but isn't required for Docker image building.
